Integral Error Criteria for Controller Tuning

Consider the closed loop shown in Figure 10.8 in [1], where Gp = 1/(5s + 1), Gv = 1/(2s + 1), Gm = 1/(s + 1), Km = 1, and Gc = Kc(1 + 1/(5s)).

Here we consider a proportional-integral controller. Set the value of the control gain Kc; the integral time is fixed (τI = 5).

The closed-loop transfer function for step point changes is given by G = Y/Ysp = Kc(1 + s)/(Kc + 5s(1 + 3s + 2s2)) (if there is no disturbance).

When a step in the set point is applied (i.e. Ysp = 1/s), the response y(t) is plotted and values of the three integral errors are given (see Snapshot 1).

These integral errors (all truncated at t = 5000 in the calculation shown here) are defined by: IAE = ∫0∞|e(t)|dt (the integral of the absolute value of the error indicated by the gray area shown in the response versus time plot), ISE = ∫0∞(e(t))2dt (the integral of the squared error), and ITAE = ∫0∞t |e(t)|dt (the integral of the time-weighted absolute error).

In addition, the Demonstration performs controller tuning by computing the values of Kc that minimize the integral errors (see Snapshots 2–4). These are shown by blue dots.

A frequency analysis shows that sustained oscillations (shown in Snapshot 5) take place when Kc = 7.5 and ω = √2/2.
